notes: These records are successive annal and retrospective references to Yelü Hongji, Emperor Daozong of Liao, who reigned from AD 1055 to 1101.
Emperor Daozong of Liao (Yelü Hongji, 遼道宗) is distinct from the seventh-century Tang prince Li Daozong (李道宗).
The annals call him Right Guard Grand Guardian Chala; Yelü Yixin's biography recounts the same accusation against Yelü Sala and names the accuser Yelü Chala.

Chala or Zhala (查剌, and the variant 劄剌) was borne by multiple Liao and Jin people. The records distinguish Emperor Daozong, Yelü Renxian, Yelü Chala, Shiwei Chala, Yelü Zizhong, two Jin people, a Zubu leader, a later Liao officer, and a hermit.
The AD 1077 annal explicitly names Right Guard Grand Guardian Chala and Shiwei Chala separately in the same sentence. Yelü Renxian died in AD 1072, before Yelü Chala's AD 1077 accusation.

The English form Liu Xin represents six distinct people here: the Western Han scholar Liu Xin (劉歆), Emperor Ai of Han (劉欣), Marquis of Yanxiang Liu Xin (劉信), the Later Han Prince of Cai Liu Xin (劉信), a tenth-century Wu general Liu Xin (劉信), and the Liang officer Liu Xin (柳昕).
